comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1, C2, C6-C10. Both evaluations find the empirical background establishing challenges to supervised learning models to be well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate citations and accurate representation of findings; peer reviewers treat these as established facts motivating the work without challenge.

Both address the NMPH theoretical framework (C11-C14) and find it supported. OpenEval focuses on the U-shaped function and BCM learning rule citations. Peer review (R2) encompasses broader claims including model architecture (C15-C16) and affirms the core mechanism, noting the model produces qualitatively matching results. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on model architecture claims C17-C22. OpenEval finds the model construction well-documented with appropriate citations. Peer review (R3) also includes implementation details C25-C27 and praises the clear writing and accessible architecture. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED without concerns.

Partial overlap on claims C25-C27 regarding the key mechanism of weakening moderately activated units. OpenEval finds this well-cited and central to the model. Peer review R3 accepts these implementation details as part of the broader architecture evaluation. Both SUPPORTED.

High agreement on Chanales et al. replication (C30-C33). OpenEval confirms the model replicates the U-shaped relationship with Figure 4A support. Peer review affirms the model produces representations fitting empirical results through stimulus similarity manipulation. Both SUPPORTED, though OpenEval also addresses C34 (asymmetric distortion) which peer R4 includes.

OpenEval R6 addresses novel prediction C34 about asymmetric distortion patterns. Peer R4 includes C34 in its evaluation of the Chanales simulation results and accepts it without challenge. Both SUPPORTED, though peer review groups this with the broader Chanales replication.

Strong agreement on boundary conditions C35-C36 (abrupt differentiation, learning rate requirements). OpenEval emphasizes Figure 6A-B support and connection to empirical data. Peer review explicitly highlights these as key contributions, with Reviewer 1 noting 'differentiation requires a high learning rate.' Both SUPPORTED.

Both address C37 (anticorrelation prediction). OpenEval finds it supported by Figure 6B showing bimodal distributions and notes it's a testable prediction. Peer review R5 explicitly values this: 'results in anti-correlated representations' as a key demonstration. Both SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on Favila et al. replication (C38-C41). OpenEval confirms the model replicates differentiation in same-face condition with Figure 8A. Peer review affirms the model manipulates shared vs distinct associations and produces fitting representations. Both SUPPORTED, treating this as one of three successful empirical replications.

Agreement on Schlichting et al. replication (C42-C46). OpenEval confirms the model captures how learning curriculum affects representational change via oscillation amplitude modulation. Peer review affirms success but notes 'hand-tuning of additional parameters' was needed, acknowledging parameter sensitivity while accepting the qualitative match. Both SUPPORTED.

Agreement on hippocampal differentiation prediction (C47-C49). OpenEval finds the prediction well-supported by cited evidence while acknowledging exceptions. Peer review R8 accepts these predictions as valuable contributions for future empirical work without challenge. Both SUPPORTED.

Agreement on sparse coding prediction (C50-C52). OpenEval finds the mechanistic prediction well-supported by multiple empirical studies. Peer review R8 accepts these predictions and their empirical support, treating them as part of valuable new predictions for future work. Both SUPPORTED.

Agreement on C53 (Wanjia et al. 2021 supporting abrupt differentiation). OpenEval treats this as strong convergent evidence for the model's predictions. Peer review accepts this connection between model predictions and empirical findings, implicitly affirming it as part of the thorough investigation. Both SUPPORTED.

Divergence on empirical support for NMPH learning rule (C54-C56). OpenEval finds convergent support from multiple methodological approaches (neurophysiology, fMRI/EEG, fMRI similarity) and rates SUPPORTED. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, noting 'the paper doesn't do any formal investigation of this learning rule or comparison with other learning rules,' suggesting stronger validation through comparison with alternatives would strengthen the argument.

Agreement on novel predictions C4-C5 (asymmetric distortion, anticorrelation). OpenEval finds these supported by simulation results throughout the manuscript as testable hypotheses. Peer review explicitly highlights these as important contributions of particular value. Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval R15 also includes C3 which peer R11 does not address.

Minor overlap on C3 (novel predictions summary). OpenEval R15 treats C3 as part of summarizing key predictions supported by simulation results. Peer R2 includes C3 in its broader evaluation of the core mechanism and theoretical framework. Both SUPPORTED, though addressing different scopes.
